source.title: Benign Overfitting in Classification: Provably Counter Label Noise with Larger Models
source.authors: Kai-Yue Wen; Jia-Ye Teng; J. Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study tests related generalization behavior and refines its scope: noisy labels can make overfitting harmful under mild overparameterization, while greater width can improve final performance. It also reports epoch-wise behavior, but not a complete fall-rise-fall test-error curve in all settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own measurements of validation performance over epochs and width, and excess risk over synthetic parameter/sample-size sweeps. Figure-only values are recorded as such. Cited findings from other work and numbers used only as theoretical assumptions are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is about benign overfitting, not double descent. Its own experiments still bear on several versions in new settings. It observes epoch-wise double descent in WideResNet16 on noisy CIFAR10 and explicitly does not see it for ResNet50 on ImageNet over 500 epochs. Final-iterate accuracy rises with width past interpolation. In SGD linear classifiers on Gaussian mixtures, excess risk is high at mild overparameterization and lower at heavy, only with label noise, and early stopping removes it. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find that with p=Θ(n), label noise makes interpolation provably harmful in GMM linear classification, while heavier overparameterization and early stopping help. They attribute the CIFAR10 vs ImageNet difference to label noise, which they test by injecting noise into CIFAR10. They also say they adopted self-training on ImageNet, but no such result appears in the text. Epoch-wise double descent under mild overparameterization is left as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper combines theoretical analysis of SGD-trained linear classifiers on Gaussian mixtures with ResNet experiments on image datasets; it is not a reproduction of the original double-descent method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with label-noise ratio and overparameterization level; the reported CIFAR10 downturn becomes sharper at higher noise, and final-iterate performance improves with width.
record.problems: Several experimental values are available only in figures, without numeric values or reported experimental uncertainty. The empirical notion of benign overfitting relies on the authors' stated proxies: training for a finite number of epochs as a proxy for infinite training, and the best-versus-last validation gap as a proxy for a generalization gap. The width ablation is repeated four times, but no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results omitted. Cited results from prior work and the PTB language-modeling overfitting observation were not recorded because they do not report a result on the claim's specified double-descent behavior.

untested.parts: Under-parameterized widths and the location of a peak at the interpolation threshold.
Not isolated or reported, though the GMM grid contains fixed-p, increasing-n slices (see missing).
Under-parameterized side and classical U-curve (only n≤p sampled); model classes beyond linear classifiers and ResNets.
Splitting into multiple peaks; tuned explicit regularization (only early stopping tested).

missing.what: Fixed-p slices of the GMM grid. Increasing n toward p moves into the mild regime with higher noisy last-epoch excess risk, a possible 'more data hurts' result. The theorem's lower bound also grows as r=p/n falls.

Extended GMM grids across SNR 5–160: harmful overfitting in mild regime is consistent, benign in heavy, and early stopping fixes it. At SNR 5, constant excess risk appears even on noiseless data at large p/n.
Transformer on PTB (Adam 4800 epochs; SGD 140 epochs): validation loss rises with training and no second descent is shown.

record.verdict_notes: The study's harmful region is the mild-overparameterization regime above interpolation, not an explicitly located interpolation-threshold peak; verdicts treat it as the double-descent bump only loosely. Most evidence is figure-only and qualitative, with no error bars. Bartlett et al. and other double-descent results are cited only and are not counted.

versions.untested_parts: The width sweep does not establish the full fall-rise-fall curve or locate a peak at the interpolation threshold.
The study does not show the complete fall-rise-fall test-error shape consistently; several reported trajectories show only a rise or fall, or a partial curve.
The synthetic sweep varies parameter size and sample size together; it does not isolate increasing sample size near a fixed interpolation threshold.
The study does not establish a complete classical U-shaped-to-second-descent curve across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location.
The study examines label-noise effects on overfitting, but does not test whether a double-descent peak is driven by noise, whether peaks split, or whether optimal regularization removes them.
The study does not re-express complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that makes a second descent an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: linear classifier trained on synthetic Gaussian mixture data
rows.size_stated: parameter dimension p swept; p and sample size n vary in the experiment
rows.operation_detail: Sweep parameter size and sample size; report excess risk for the final-epoch classifier.
rows.value: Figure-only; the text says the noiseless experiment does not cause overfitting.
rows.note: The plotted sweep jointly varies p and n, so it does not isolate a one-dimensional capacity curve.
rows.check: Noiseless GMM shows no harmful region at any p/n, consistent with the peak being noise-driven. It shows no capacity effect, so it is not V4 evidence. The grid is 2D (n≤p, both 2^4–2^9), so p/n is a readable capacity axis; it is not a confounded joint sweep.

rows.subject: linear classifier trained on synthetic Gaussian mixture data
rows.size_stated: parameter dimension p swept; p and sample size n vary in the experiment
rows.operation_detail: Sweep parameter size and sample size; report excess risk for the final-epoch classifier.
rows.value: Figure-only; the text reports overfitting with mild overparameterization and benign overfitting in the heavy regime.
rows.note: The text distinguishes mild from heavy overparameterization, but p and n are swept together and the full curve is not reported.
rows.check: V4: risk improves as p/n grows from mild to heavy, but only the overparameterized side is sampled (n≤p), so no first descent or peak is shown. V6 (noise drives the harm): observed. Baseline should be the noiseless grid R1, not the mild regime.

rows.subject: linear classifier trained on synthetic Gaussian mixture data
rows.size_stated: parameter dimension p swept; p and sample size n vary in the experiment
rows.operation_detail: Sweep parameter size and sample size; report excess risk for the best classifier through training.
rows.value: Figure-only; the text says early stopping can effectively avoid overfitting.
rows.note: Early stopping is a comparison condition; the plotted sweep does not isolate sample-size effects.
rows.check: The early-stopped classifier avoids the excess risk in the noisy mild regime, i.e. regularization by early stopping removes it. This is not V4 evidence; baseline is the final-epoch noisy classifier R2.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Measure training and validation performance over 500 epochs.
rows.baseline: best model occurs in the middle of training
rows.value: The paper states that test loss increased as the model further fit the training set; it reports no similar double-descent phenomenon in this 500-epoch experiment.
rows.note: The text describes a mid-training best and subsequent deterioration, not a later second descent.
rows.check: Authors state they do not observe epoch-wise double descent on ImageNet in 500 epochs; only mid-training best then worse test loss. Note the schedule restarts at epoch 90 with LR 1e-3, a possible confound.

relation.reason: Its own training trajectories, width comparisons, noise interventions and early-stopping analysis bear directly on versions of the claim.

tranche.reason: The study supplies its own results in Gaussian-mixture classification and image-classification settings, including positive and negative epoch-wise observations. Its central question concerns benign overfitting rather than a reproduction or general refutation of double descent.

source_check.notes: Section 4.1 reverses error and accuracy in one sentence; its final paragraph and Figure 3 caption consistently describe accuracy increasing then decreasing. ImageNet training changes schedule after epoch 90; the conclusion mentions self-training without presenting a corresponding result.
